recipes.name: Bubble and Squeak
ingredients_raw: 3 cups potatoes - baked, cooled and thinly sliced

steps.text: Cook cabbage in a medium saucepan with a small amount of water until tender, about 3 to 5 minutes. Drain, and set aside.
Cook bacon and onion in a well-seasoned cast iron skillet until onion is soft and bacon is cooked, about 5 minutes.
Add ham, and cook until heated through. Add butter, then mix in cooked cabbage and potatoes; season with paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned on the bottom, turn, and brown again.

raw_recipe.headline: Bubble and Squeak
raw_recipe.description: Bubble and squeak is a delicious way to use leftover potatoes, cabbage, or any veggies for a comforting side dish that makes the most of leftovers.

review.reviewBody: Bubble and Squeak is a traditional English dish that is usually served on Boxing Day (December 26). Obviously, you can have it any time of the year, but the idea is that you smoosh up and skillet-fry together the veggies left over from the Christmas Day main meal, ie. peas, roast potatoes, carrots, cabbage and brussel sprouts. I know this because I have eaten it every December 26 for the last 30 years! It takes its name from the noise it makes while cooking. It doesn't smell especially wonderful while cooking, but the end result is absolutely delicious!

what a tasty dish! i wanted it as a side so i only used the bacon. i did not have leftovers except for baked potatoes so i chopped rhutabagas and cooked in chicken stock till 1/3rd done, added carrots until almost done, and the added cabbage. the veggies sucked up almost all the stock so they they very tasty. i crisped bacon in a nonstick pan, took out and diced, poured off fat,and sauteed chopped onions, added garlic, then added strained and tossed veggies and chopped potatoes, the diced bacon, and chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. i drizzled on olive oil which made it down to the bottom of the pan and then smashed it down with a spatula. i browned it and used a plate on top of frying pan to invert and put back in pan to brown the other side. i then added a splash of balsamic vinegar when done. what a super combination of flavors!! thanks!

We used dehydrated cheesy scalloped potatoes to save time. We added 2-3 shredded carrots and a dash of cayenne spice for heat. We topped the dish with more grated cheddar cheese and placed under the broiler for 30 seconds to get a toasty cheese topping. We served each portion with a fried egg on top. It’s not traditional, but we also added some chopped pepperoni and salami to add some zing. Yum!

I steamed the cabbage. Made the thick cut bacon (4 slices, because it's bacon) in the oven until almost completely done. The used scissors to cut it into small pieces. This went into the large skillet prepared with about a half TBSP of olive oil. Used paprika and pepper, but not salt because bacon and ham have enough.
I much prefer the traditional way of making this dish of using mashed potatoes and some roughly chopped up roast potatoes, fries perfectly together and is great with British gravy or HP brown sauce

My first review here. I made it. I really hate deviating from a recipe the first time I make something, but I had to make some changes due to what I had on hand. Instead of ham and bacon, I used 4 links of Italian sausage that I removed from the casings and crumbled up during cooking. Used 1/4 package of bacon that I also cut up as it was cooking into small pieces. Added a green bell pepper along with the onion. Used a whole head of cabbage instead of 1/2. Didn't have any left over baked potatoes, so I cooked 2 in microwave, let them cool and then sliced them up. It made a HUGE amount. It took a lot longer than I expected to cook because I used the whole head of cabbage and it wouldn't fit in the frying pan so I had to cook it up in 3 smaller batches and then combine after it was all cooked. I also had so much in my big frying pan at the end that I couldn't really flip it over for blowing as the recipe said to do. I had to just flip small sections over and even doing that was hard with as much as I had in the pan. I was worried how it was going to taste with so much time and food I used, but it turned out great. We are looking forward to having the left overs for few days to come. I will make this again.

Traditionally a Boxing Day cleanup of leftovers, however I also make it the day after St. Pat's Day to use up leftovers from Corned Beef & Cabbage and I use chopped Corned Beef rather than bacon or ham, Onions, leeks or scallions are sauted in rendered fat from the Corned Beef, then add in cabbage potatoes, carrots & CB. Always in a well seasoned cast iron skillet. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Serve with toast and fried eggs..... MM..MM..GOOD!!
Love the ingredients. I will do it meatless then fry up a prok chop or fix hash with it. I like the idea of using more mashed potatoes.
I made this before. But I use sausage like polish sausage. Instead of bacon. I make it once or twice a week.

Another one for the It'sa keeper column. This was delicious. I omitted the ham (I don't care for it) and increased the bacon. I cooked the onion and cabbage till it had a lot of brown caramelization. Hubbs loved it. Adding it to our favorites and will make it again and again.

Hands down easy. Made as written the first time. It was good but the second time I gave it a " Finnish" twist. I added 3-5 tbsp of pure maple syrup and lots of salt n pepper and baked it in a big casserole dish for an hr at 350. Now my family requests this especially when we have worked outside cutting wood or shovelling snow during the winter.

I've heard of this British food dish through British videos and always wondered what it was. Now I know. I didn't have any ham leftovers so I just used extra bacon cut into chunks. Next time I make this I will use mashed potatoes as that sounds really tasty, too. Definitely a keeper as it's filling and low budget which is definitely needed these days.

I made this with leftover mashed potatoes and a piece of ham that was also leftover, as well as bacon. It was quite salty. It needed more cabbage than I used. I'll probably make it again with some of the suggestions from others.
My Mam used to make bubble and squeak for teatime using up leftovers from Sunday lunch gorgeous
Love this one. I make this every time we have ham left overs.

I made this last night with a few tweaks here and there. I basically threw everything together in a big pan after I fried the bacon. I added some water to the bottom of the pan and let summer flipping it consistently. The flavor was pretty bland so I tossed in some minced garlic. I must've done something right. The hubs had two helpings.
We all loved it, I might be adding more veggies next time, but flavors was great!
Delicious! Didn't really brown in my iron skillet, but I didn't care. I'm thinking of adding some green & red peppers to leftovers.
